title: What rule makes the water in Tanvi's tank go down?
description: Tanvi reads the litres left in a village water tank each hour. The video finds how much goes out each hour and carries the row on three more hours.
teaching_notes: One idea: when the numbers fall, the rule takes away the same amount each time. Watch for children who add because the jump is a number.

source: Find the rule and write the next three numbers: 9,000, 8,500
video_script.why: The child has seen a row that grows by the same jump and now meets a row that falls.
video_script.substitution: Take the smaller reading from the larger one; the same answer every time is the amount taken away, and taking it from the last number gives the next ones.
video_script.anchor: a rooftop water tank in Tanvi's village in Kerala, read every hour
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu sees the jump of five hundred and says add it. The readings get smaller, so the rule must take away.
video_script.payoff_line: the rule is take away five hundred

final_answer.value: The rule is subtract 500; the next numbers are 7,000, 6,500 and 6,000
final_answer.spoken: take away five hundred, then seven thousand, six thousand five hundred and six thousand

maths_rules: the readings fall by 500 every time, so the rule is subtract 500
slip: add 500 would make 9,000 + 500 = 9,500, which is bigger, but the next reading is smaller
video_script.design: One idea: a falling row has a take-away rule. Wrong idea: add the jump. The tank readings sit in a row with arrows pointing down in size; the labels arrive in the idea part.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>A water tank stands on a roof in Tanvi's village in Kerala. She reads the litres left every hour.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>Her readings are nine thousand, eight thousand five hundred, eight thousand and seven thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Find the rule and write the next three numbers.

beats.on_screen: the anchor holds still and gets an accent underline

marks.stop: the anchor is underlined in the accent colour

narration: <bookmark mark='stop'/>Stop the video. Say your answer out loud.

beats.on_screen: the four readings sit in a row; an arrow joins each reading to the next; each arrow has an empty label

marks.row: the four readings sit in a row with arrows between them
marks.ask: an empty label appears on every arrow

narration: <bookmark mark='row'/>Look at the row of readings. Each reading is joined to the next by an arrow.
<bookmark mark='jump'/>Each arrow is one hour.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>For every arrow, ask two things. Does the water go up or down, and by how many litres?

beats.on_screen: Chintu's bubble shows add 500; each reading is smaller than the one before; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.small: each reading glows smaller than the one before
marks.strike: the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>Every jump is five hundred, so the rule is add five hundred.
<bookmark mark='small'/>Adding makes a number bigger. Look at the readings again. Each one is smaller than the one before.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>The rule cannot be an adding rule.

beats.on_screen: each arrow gets its label −500; the board reads 9,000 − 8,500 = 500, 8,500 − 8,000 = 500, 8,000 − 7,500 = 500; the rule card reads subtract 500

marks.take: the board opens with the words larger reading take away smaller
marks.rule: the rule card reading subtract 500 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Take away the smaller reading from the larger one.
<bookmark mark='a'/>Nine thousand take away eight thousand five hundred leaves five hundred.
<bookmark mark='b'/>Eight thousand five hundred take away eight thousand leaves five hundred.
<bookmark mark='c'/>Eight thousand take away seven thousand five hundred leaves five hundred.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The readings fall by the same amount, so the rule is take away five hundred.

beats.on_screen: from the last reading 7,500 three new boxes fill in turn: 7,000, 6,500, 6,000; the answer card lists them

marks.one: the first empty box fills with 7,000
marks.two: the second empty box fills with 6,500
marks.three: the third empty box fills with 6,000

narration: <bookmark mark='start'/>Start from the last reading, seven thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Take away five hundred to reach seven thousand.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Take away five hundred again to reach six thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Take away five hundred once more to reach six thousand.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The next three numbers are seven thousand, six thousand five hundred and six thousand.

beats.on_screen: the stage clears except the tank; two lines appear: a falling row has a take-away rule; take the rule from the last number to go on; then a new row 12,000, 11,800, 11,600 and three empty boxes

marks.one: the line a falling row has a take-away rule appears
marks.two: the line take the rule from the last number appears
marks.turn: a new row 12,000, 11,800, 11,600 appears with three empty boxes

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>If the numbers fall, the rule takes the same amount away each time.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Take the rule away from the last number to go on.
<bookmark mark='turn'/>Your turn. A tank reads twelve thousand, eleven thousand eight hundred, eleven thousand six hundred. What is the rule, and what are the next three readings?
